tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local continuation of the prior F10/R10 checkpoint. Provider state remains fixed at O5/D5/I7 with mapping I7->K5@g8 and provider proof P_I7_g8. Repository claim authority is current at F10; R10 is already committed once and historical R9 remains available only as stale evidence. The fixture tests repository finalization retry/idempotency and the minimum atomic compare-and-set predicate needed to avoid a duplicate repository finalization transition. It does not test a concrete provider, external side-effect exactly-once behavior, public sources, hosted coordination, richer-mode arbitration, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledgers, scheduler state, or a second semantic leaf.

cases.observation: Current claim fence is F10 and the finalization slot already contains an exact digest match for R10.
cases.required_action: Return idempotent replay/no-op; do not perform a second finalization effect and do not rewrite the slot merely to acknowledge the retry.

cases.observation: Candidate fence F9 differs from current claim fence F10.
cases.required_action: Reject before any finalization effect even though provider mapping/proof/effect digest remain unchanged.

cases.observation: The finalization slot already contains R10, not the exact candidate digest.
cases.required_action: Return conflict/no effect; never treat shared operation identity and fence alone as sufficient for replay equivalence.

fixture.minimum_safe_cas_rule: Scope the finalization slot by exact {operation,payload,idempotency_identity}. First acceptance may transition only when current_claim_fence == candidate_fence and finalization_slot == ABSENT, atomically writing the full fence-bound record. Retry classification must also require current_claim_fence == candidate_fence: if finalization_slot == digest(candidate_full_record), return idempotent no-op; if the slot is nonempty but differs, return conflict/no effect. Therefore the minimum mutable compare set is {current_claim_fence, finalization_slot_state_or_exact_record_digest} with the slot key carrying {operation,payload,idempotency_identity}; the committed value must bind provider mapping generation, provider proof identity, effect digest and fence. Fence equality alone is insufficient, and finalization-record equality without a current-fence check becomes stale after a later fence advance.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: Any finalization candidate with the same operation/idempotency identity and current fence can be treated as a harmless retry.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: A same-F10 candidate with different mapping/proof/effect digest would be collapsed into R10 and could authorize a distinct effect. Exact committed-record equivalence is required for no-op replay; otherwise the attempt is a conflict.

observations: Exact R10 replay under still-current F10 is safely classifiable as a no-op only when the stored finalization record matches the candidate exactly.
R9 remains rejected before effect because repository authority is stale even though provider evidence is unchanged.
A conflicting candidate under the same F10 cannot be deduplicated by operation/fence alone; record-level equivalence is necessary.

The first-write atomic guard can be expressed as current fence equality plus an ABSENT finalization slot scoped by operation/payload/idempotency identity; replay requires current fence equality plus exact stored-record digest equality.
inference: Within the tested repository-finalization scope, a recurring-Chat pool can obtain duplicate-safe finalization without hosted arbitration by combining a monotonic claim fence with a per-operation finalization slot and exact-record replay semantics. The fixture narrows the minimal state needed for the repository transition, but does not prove exactly-once behavior for an external side effect occurring outside that atomic repository mutation.
unresolved_children: Test a two-writer same-F10 race against an initially ABSENT finalization slot: one candidate should win the atomic transition, an identical loser should reduce to exact-record no-op, and a conflicting loser should fail closed; verify which fields must be read and compared in one atomic repository primitive.
Test behavior after a later fence F11: exact historical R10 must cease to be retry-authorizing despite record equality, while provider evidence may remain provenance.
